title: More than 100,000 People in Japan Are 100 or Older
paragraphs: There are now more than 100,000 people in Japan who are 100 years old or older, according to data from the country's health ministry. It's the first time this number has gone above 100,000.
The country's total number of centenarians is actually 107,677. That's an increase of nearly 8,000 from last year.
Almost 95,000 of those centenarians are women.
"I am very pleased that so many people are remaining active and healthy for so long," said health minister Kenichiro Ueno.
Japan has one of the world's oldest populations, and the number of centenarians in the country has been increasing for some time.
The government started collecting data on centenarians in 1963. At that time, there were just 153 people in Japan who were 100 or older.
By 1981, there were over 1,000. And by 2012, there were more than 50,000.
Everyone who turns 100 in Japan receives a letter and a gift from the prime minister. Over 54,000 people are expected to turn 100 before March 31 of next year.
Right now, Japan's oldest person is Kyoto resident Fuyo Kishimoto, who is 114 years old. The oldest man in the country is 112-year-old Hikaru Kato, who lives in Kumamoto on the island of Kyushu.
It's believed that people in Japan live so long because they do things like stay active and eat well.
However, the country actually has too many old people and not enough young ones. About 30% of Japan's population is now 65 and older — and that's expected to increase to 40% by 2070.
